steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper.

Beat egg whites, vanilla, and cream of tartar in a glass, metal, or ceramic bowl until soft peaks form. Slowly add sugar and continue to beat until stiff peaks form and mixture becomes glossy. Fold in cocoa powder and chocolate chips. Drop mixture by teaspoonfuls onto the prepared cookie sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool to room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Meringue Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These deliciously light chocolate meringue cookies have double the chocolaty taste, thanks to the addition of cocoa powder and semisweet chips.
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate Meringue Cookies

review.reviewBody: I made one batch of these and they were flat as pancakes but that was totally my fault. They tasted good so I read a little tutorial on whipping egg whites and made a second batch that came out great. The first time I used cold egg whites, wasn't that careful about separating and started on high speed which I know now is all wrong. Thanks for a great recipe and a good learning experience.

After I'd read others' reviews, I used 2 Tbsp cocoa and only 1/2 cup sugar in my cookies; choc chips were omitted. Just the right sweetness and chocolatey-ness for me. On top of that, I didn't follow the instructions verbatim. I adapted instructions from other meringue cookie recipes to suit this recipe instead. First, beat in cream of tartar and vanilla when the egg whites become foamy; continue whipping till soft peaks form. When soft peaks form, gradually beat in sugar (a little at a time) to egg whites till they form stiff peaks and look glossy. I folded in cocoa lastly--don't overfold the mixture. Since this was my first attempt at making meringue, I was slightly worried. I wondered whether combining vanilla and cream of tartar with egg whites first will actually prevent the the egg whites from "growing" in volume. Separate the egg whites from the yolks right after the eggs are out of refrigerator. Then, wait to start baking when the egg whites get to room temperature. Also, make sure you use only grease-free metal or glass mixing bowl and beeaters for whipping egg whites. Finally, these cookies took longer to get done (for me), about 35~40 minutes; they're done when the tops of the cookies are kind of hard. I got about 36~40 of them with a teaspoonfuls for each. Overall, this is a wonderful choc meringue drop recipe--definitely a keeper! The best part is they're lower in calories than other cookies!

I think these are one of those "stupid simple" recipes. I did not add the chocolate chips but did increase the cooca (Hershey's Dark) by 1/2 Tablespoon. I piped these out to look like kisses and baked for 20 minutes only and let cool. Once cool they melted in my mouth. I had only made these because I had some egg whites I had to use but these are going in my "cookie" gift boxes. I used my KitchenAid mixer and beat the egg whites until they were "dry" and folded in the cocoa.....easy, BUT you have to make sure you beat the egg whites really good. THANK YOU FOR SHARING....yum!

Turned out great. Here are my notes for next time I make it:

(1) Separate egg whites while cold, then let the whites come to room temperature before beating
(2) Use superfine sugar (if you have it)
(3) Use a Silpat or parchment paper instead of greasing cookie sheets
(4) Cook in oven at 250F (lower temp) for 40 min, then turn oven off and let it sit in the oven closed for 1 hour
(5) I'd probably omit the chocolate chips next time.

One more tip:
They don't spread out while baking, so you can put them really close together on the cookie sheet.

These were delicious! Be sure the egg whites are at room temperature, beat them at medium speed until frothy, then add the cream of tartar and vanilla, and slowly add the sugar. Put the meringue in a large ziploc bag, cut off the corner and pipe onto the parchment lined baking sheet. After the meringues are baked, shut off the oven and let them cool down and dry out for a couple of hours. Also good without the cocoa for plain meringues and you can sprinkle them with coloured sugar.

These were yummy! I modified based on the suggestions of another reviewer. I reduced the sugar to 1/2 cup, boubled the cocoa (I used Frys), and upped the chips to 1/2 cup. I added the cream of tartar and vanilla to the foamy eggy whites, and once I had soft peaks, I started slowly adding the sugar to a running mixer. I was worried when I lost some volume while folding in the cocoa and chips, but they still turned out great. I've been looking for a way to use up egg whites when I need a lot of yolks for home made ice cream. Most ice cream recipes call for 8 yolks, so next time, I will try doubling this recipe to use up 6/8 egg whites.

I made this one night out of boredom. My 8 year old daughter took some to school the next morning and she also ate four before leaving! She came home and said mom we need more! My friends love those cookies! The only thing I would say I did different would be the chocolate chips… I have large chocolate chips from Sam’s so they would have been too big. I put them in my blender for a few seconds and mixed some in the batter then sprinkled some on top. I wish I had the pic of that. They turned out amazing I made this recipe three times in a week my family loved it so much lol! It’s a keeper!

My granddaughter made these, with a little help from grandma, and they turned out pretty good 
We did change sugar to 1/2 cup, and added 2 tablespoons of cocoa. We actually had no cream of tarter, so we substituted 1/4 tsp of lemon juice. We will make these again!

I got ahead of myself and, knowing better than to do it, I added the cocoa powder before the eggs were fully whipped. Cocoa powder has oil in it so the eggs never beat to fully stiff. They were a little gloopy when piping but they came out tasting really good. Just a little more looking like macaroons than merengue cookies. I’ll make them again but I’ll whip them fully before adding cocoa, I’ll use a little less sugar and I’ll add a pinch of salt to counteract the sweet. I like strong dark chocolate so the changes will make them perfect for me and my crew.

I made these for a cookie exchange at work and everyone loved them. I watched a You Tube video on how to make meringue cookies and it said the key is to add the sugar a tablespoon at a time and beat it until you can no longer feel any grains when you rub a little of the batter between your fingers. It also said to get that crunchy outside/soft inside taste you should bake the cookies at 300 degrees, turn off the oven and let the cookies sit in there for at least an hour as the oven cools. I also took the advice of another user here to use less sugar so I only used 1/2 c rather than the full 2/3 c and they were delicious! Definitely sweet enough with the 1/2 c. If my daughter had her way I would be making these once a week! Enjoy!

This recipe was great! Like the others, I made some changes. I used only 1/3 cups of sugar and two tablespoons of cocoa powder. I also omitted the chocolate chips since it sounds sweet enough without them. I didn't have any cream of tartar so I substituted with 1/4 tsp. of lemon juice. It worked perfectly fine. I recommend anyone who hasn't really made meringue or whipped eggs before: separate eggs when they're cold (it's easier), let them come to room temperature (around at least 30 mins, possibly more), and avoid using plastic bowls. Add the sugar slowly, too. It can take around 5min for the eggs, so be patient! The baking time took at least an hour for me too, but I suppose it's dependent on every one's oven. I found that it's easier when you make smaller cookies, the larger ones I made take a little longer to bake (smaller cookies - around an hour).
Super easy to make and yummy!!!
I’ve been looking for this recipe after misplaced it somewhere In my phone. Who knows where! They are delicious and I make them every Christmas.
Made these using almond extract instead of vanilla . Otherwise didn’t change a thing and they turned out great. I used a stand mixer and my whites were cold and they still whipped up beautifully.
These were fun to make with the niece and nephew. They were also demolished in minutes. I even doubled the recipe. I have many Celiac Disease members of the family, and these were a huge hit.

Was trying to beat the eggs by hand, the instructions definitely tell you to put the sugar in way too early if you're trying to do that. Never got past soft peaks, put them in the oven anyway :/ still waiting to find out how they actually taste but I stole small tastes from the bowl as I whisked, I think the plain vanilla meringue is better than the chocolate in my opinion, though you probably shouldn't eat raw meringue...

it was really good. chewy on the ourside, soft on the inside, but it left out some usful tips that i really needed. i mean overall delish but we had to guess on a few things, and got it right. MORE DETAILS PLEASE!!! 🙏
Excellent! I followed the recipient exactly and these are delicious! Next time I will try using a nocalorie sweetener to see if I can reduce the calorie content.

These were great, the only change I made was that I added a little more cocoa powder. They reminded me a little of cocoa puffs. After baking, turn off the oven and leave the cookies in it to cool. This will prevent the cookies from sinking.

We sometimes purchase meringue cookies from the grocery store (when they have them), so today, my son asked if I would try making some. If I had known how incredibly easy they were, I would have been making them all along. These aren't identical to the grocery store ones, but they are delicious! These are a little lighter and airier than grocery-store ones, which are a little crunchier and denser. I followed the recipe exactly, and for me, these didn't spread - they kept their shape nicely. I will definitely make them again.
